_comment: THE TYPE TOKEN IS DERIVED FROM THE ELEMENT, NOT FROM ITS TAG.
Before 2026-07-30 the model carried BOTH a `circle` kind and an `ellipse`
kind, and the token was whichever one the SVG tag had produced. That is
PROVENANCE, not geometry: apply_scale composes a matrix onto
common.transform and never touches the radii, so a `circle` element stays
typed `circle` while being drawn as an egg, and an `ellipse` with equal
radii is round while answering `ellipse`. The Layers filter's Circle
checkbox therefore answered 'which tag did this arrive as', which is not a
JYH ruled 2026-07-30: one round kind in the model. `circle` survives as a
DERIVED token -- rx == ry -- so the checkbox finally means 'is it round'.
AS AUTHORED, DELIBERATELY. The token ignores common.transform, because NO
type token accounts for transforms: a sheared rect is still `rect`, a
rotated text is still `text`. Making `circle` the one token that consults
the matrix would be a second rule nobody could predict from the first.

rows.why: authored as <circle r=20>; parses to an ellipse with rx == ry == 20, and reads back as round
authored as <ellipse rx=20 ry=20>; identical geometry, so it MUST answer identically -- this is the row the old tag-based token got wrong
